title: Attenuated fanout throttler with phase-based degradation for downstream resilience
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: During bursts or partial downstream failure (eg. Redis/Kafka latency spikes, DB saturation) our existing per-request fanout causes cascading queue growth and exhausted connection pools in regional proxies. This ticket implements an "attenuated fanout throttler" that limits the effective fanout per incoming model request and degrades request handling in deterministic phases to preserve SLOs and reduce tail amplification across regions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New throttler enforces a configurable per-request fanout cap and global windowed concurrency. 2) Phase-based degradation triggers (soft -> moderate -> strict) based on downstream health signals (p99 latency, error-rate, conn-usage) and are observable in Console. 3) No customer-facing 5xx increase beyond explained and documented degradation for 5% of synthetic traffic during chaos runs. 4) Rollout feature flagged and gradable per-tenant; e2e tests and benchmark harness show reduced peak connection usage by >=40% under simulated downstream failure while keeping median latency increase <=20ms for P1 tenants.
implementation_notes: Design summary: 1) Admission controller intercepts requests before fanout and computes a per-tenant effective fanout budget using tenant priority, recent success score, and global congestion score. 2) Throttler implements three phases: SOFT (reduce non-critical fanout like non-blocking prefetches), MODERATE (collapse background hedges, reduce parallelism), STRICT (serialize dependent calls and serve cached/stale responses). 3) Connection pool integration: borrow tokens from a new fanout token bucket that maps to pool slots; if tokens exhausted, route to degradation policy. 4) Health signals: integrate Redis/Kafka/DB probes + pool fill ratio + p99 latency from infra metrics. 5) Policy config stored in runtime-config with sharding by region for low-latency evaluation.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Shadow mode for 2 weeks in canary region (us-west-2) with metrics collection. 3) Gradual enable for non-critical tenants (10% -> 30% -> 60%) over 2 sprints. 4) If error-rate or SLO regressions observed, auto-rollback to shadow or disable phase escalation. 5) Post-rollout: enable for P1 tenants with conservative defaults, monitor for 48h.
monitoring_and_slos: Metrics: per-tenant fanout_count, fanout_reduced_count, tokens_acquired, pool_fill_ratio, degradation_phase, downstream_p99_ms, downstream_error_rate. Dashboards: per-region and per-tenant views. Alerts: firing when downstream_p99_ms > 200ms for 5m AND degradation_phase != SOFT; SLO change: add a secondary SLO for tail preservation (P99 latency budget) that the throttler is intended to protect. Logging: structured events for each phase transition and reason code.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token bucket, phase transitions, and config parsing. Integration tests against local redis/kafka/db harness. Chaos tests: inject p99-latency and connection starvation; validate connection usage and SLOs. Load tests: benchmark with synthetic traffic (50k rps) to measure pool usage reduction. Add regression eval to Redwood Optimize nightly job to detect quality regressions caused by aggressive fanout collapse.
